nodes.label: Scatter / Gather
nodes.rationale: Single-key storage of a collection means one upstream failure wipes every cached entry at once and partial recovery is impossible. Scatter/gather stores each entity under its own key. It is the most involved feature, so the guidance is to default to single-key @Failover unless per-entity slicing (independent expiry/recovery, partial recovery) is genuinely needed.

nodes.label: Parallel slice dispatch (virtual threads)
nodes.rationale: Per-entity store/recover run as a CompletableFuture per slice on virtual threads by default; sequential mode exists for debugging and low-throughput scenarios.

nodes.label: Per-slice timeout (failover.scatter.timeout)
nodes.rationale: Without a bound, one hung slice (e.g. exhausted JDBC pool) blocks the business thread indefinitely on join(). On recover the timeout is per slice and a timed-out slice counts as not recovered so the rest still merges; on store it bounds aggregate completion (allOf().orTimeout()) and already-completed writes are not rolled back. Ignored when parallel=false because inline slices cannot be interrupted.

nodes.label: Partial Recovery Behaviour
nodes.rationale: The framework never filters nulls — merge owns the null policy — and only short-circuits to null when every slice is empty. Partial recovery is logged as a WARN and metered via failover.recovery.partial.total so it is never silent. In some domains an incomplete collection is more dangerous than a clean failure because the caller cannot tell it is incomplete, so rejecting the whole composite is a documented option.

nodes.label: recoverAll semantics (four rules)
nodes.rationale: shouldRecoverAll = args == null || args.isEmpty() || recoverAll(). recoverAll affects only the recover path (store always splits); empty args recover-all automatically; id args need no flag; filter args must force recoverAll=true or the filters would be wrongly split into entity keys. recoverAll without a payloadSplitter does nothing and logs a startup WARN.

nodes.label: N-slice recover-all deduplication rule
nodes.rationale: doRecoverAll calls recoverSliceForAll per context; with the default handler recoverAll ignores args and returns all entries by name, so N contexts produce N x all-entries. splitOnRecover must therefore return exactly one placeholder unless a custom delegateR.recoverAll partitions by the context args.

nodes.label: Two-splitter pattern (batch-by-id + findAll on one domain)
nodes.rationale: A method with id args and a separate findAll() need different recover strategies, so they use two PayloadSplitter beans but share a domain — each populates entries the other can recover.

nodes.label: PayloadSplitterExecutionException
nodes.rationale: Wraps any user-splitter failure with operation, splitter bean name, failover name, full annotation config and original cause, so a splitter bug is diagnosable from logs without a debugger.

edges.source_location: A timed-out slice is indistinguishable from a cache miss at merge time
